newsitem.title: USA: Western Resources drops bid; Tyco, ADT complete deal.
newsitem.headline: Western Resources drops bid; Tyco, ADT complete deal.

text.p: Kansas utility Western Resources Inc. said Wednesday it was dropping its $3.9 billion hostile bid for ADT Ltd., clearing the way for the electronic security giant to complete its friendly $5.7 billion merger with Tyco International Ltd.

Western, which owns 27 percent of ADT, said it will reap a $710 million gain on its conversion of ADT shares into Tyco stock. It also said it will pursue a Bermuda court action against ADT related to the value of its ADT holdings.

The Topeka, Kan.-based utility had been expected to drop the stock and cash bid, which valued ADT at $22.50 per share. Last month, it cancelled a June 17 shareholders meeting on the proposed acquisition.
ADT disclosed in May that it was in talks with Western about dropping the bid, but Western had never confirmed those discussions.

Western launched its takeover effort in December after slowly amassing a big stake in Bermuda-based ADT. The bid was widely considered too low for a company that is a key player in the booming electronic security industry.
ADT then announced a friendly all-stock transaction with Tyco in March. Under that agreement, shareholders of ADT received 0.48133 shares of the combined company for each share of ADT stock held.
Shareholders of both Tyco, based in Exeter, N.H., and ADT on Wednesday approved the transaction, which values ADT at $36.43 per share.

The deal will create a security giant that provides fire protection, detection and security systems and services to industrial, commercial and residential customers in more than 50 countries. Tyco's new fire and safety services segment will have sales of over $4.5 billion.
Industrial conglomerate Tyco has been one of the nation's most acquisitive companies this year.

Western Resources stock closed down 19 cents at $32.56 and ADT gained $2.50 to $36.25, both in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Tyco jumped $4.44 to end at $75.25, also on the NYSE.

Meanwhile, Western said it will continue to pursue growth prospects in the electronic security industry, although it declined to discuss its strategy. The company, which late last year bought the electronic security business of Westinghouse Electric Corp., has plenty of potential partners in the highly fragmented and consolidating industry.
"Western has pretty deep pockets and they'll find something else to buy," said David Bitterman of Bear Stearns & Co Inc.

Despite the loss of ADT, Western is considered to be a savvy and aggressive buyer. The company last year launched a rare hostile takeover in the utility industry and, after a 10-month fight, wrested target Kansas City Power & Light Co. from a planned merger with UtiliCorp United Inc.
